newsitem.title: INDIA: HG Asia says subscribe to India Bank of Baroda IPO.
newsitem.headline: HG Asia says subscribe to India Bank of Baroda IPO.

text.p: Securities firm HG Asia on Wednesday recommended investors subscribe to the initial public offering of India's state-run Bank of Baroda due to open next week.
HG Asia analyst Rajeev Varma said competitive valuations, a substantial improvement in asset quality and lack of capital adequacy concerns after the issue made the IPO stock a good investment.
"The bank has shown a significant improvement in its asset quality. That gives us the confidence that the bank is serious about cleaning up its balance sheet," Varma said.
Bank of Baroda's IPO 8.5 billion rupee issue is scheduled to open on December 5.
Varma said net non-performing assets were forecast to fall below 3.9 percent by 1998/99 (April-March) from the current 7.8 percent.
He said after the IPO the bank would not have any capital adequacy concerns.
"This will enable Bank of Baroda to leverage its strength and grow in a sector which is still largely undercapitalised," Varma said in a report to investors.

"Being the country's second largest bank and with over 50 percent of its business coming from Gujarat and Maharashtra the bank is well-positioned to participate in the country's economic development... Subscribe to the IPO."
Varma said the bank had increased its deposit base to 284 billion rupees in 1995/96 from 190 billion in 1991/92 on the strength of its rural connection and large branch network.
"However, Bank of Baroda has lost out to competition from new private banks resulting in its market share dropping from 7.2 percent during 1991/92 to 6.3 percent last year," he said.
Varma forecast a deposit growth of 13 percent during the current year climbing to 14 percent in 1997/98 and 1998/99.
He said advances were likely to grow at an annual 15 percent during 1997/98 and 1998/99.
"However, in the current year we forecast advances growth to be far lower at 12 percent due to the sluggish credit offtake so far," he said.
Varma forecast spreads would decline to 3.71 percent in 1996/97 but increase to 3.80 percent in 1997/98 and 3.83 percent in 1998/99.
